conditional_findings.severity: unassigned; conditional selected-config divergence in source, no runtime or visual result
conditional_findings.classification: New 95e source-derived review-fixture configuration authority candidate; earlier quickstep source question is related, final aliases remain open.
conditional_findings.trace: The viewer CLI accepts a tactical combat and animation YAML, builds the fixed clock from that selected sample rate, installs the validated runtime snapshot and passes the selected TacticalCombatConfig to run. But quickstep_action_ticks, quickstep_push_ticks, quickstep planar-speed construction, release and vertical-state helpers each obtain TacticalCombatConfig::default(), whose compiled canonical YAML is independent of an alternate selected file. The planned dodge contact and fixture motion therefore use default maneuver/motor values while animation sampling uses the selected runtime rate. The authoritative server begin_authoritative_quickstep instead passes its supplied config's quickstep duration to the same contact-tick conversion.
conditional_findings.symbolic_case: Keep the compiled canonical YAML and 64 Hz rate unchanged except that a supplied valid configuration uses quickstep_duration_seconds = 1.0 instead of canonical 0.50. PositiveAnimationDuration admits both; the inspected aggregate validation has no additional check of that field. The conversion gives canonical 0.50 × 64 = 32 complete ticks and midpoint 16, versus selected 1.0 × 64 = 64 complete ticks and midpoint 32. Under the selected plan path the viewer starts its fixture dodge at midpoint 16, while the authoritative constructor given the 1.0-second config uses midpoint 32. This is symbolic source arithmetic, not a loaded YAML file, execution, pose, gameplay event or screenshot.
conditional_findings.limits: When the selected configuration agrees with the compiled defaults, this duration mismatch does not arise. Other alternate motor fields and the 93.9 kg fixture versus 94.9 kg canonical-burden constants require separate intended-character and physics-policy tracing; no actual player movement, GPU or image effect is claimed. The 72-frame fixture limit and all aliases remain open.
conditional_findings.first_failed_contract: A review intended to represent the selected runtime quickstep configuration takes its maneuver duration and motor inputs from a second, compiled default authority.
conditional_findings.canonical_owner: The explicitly selected TacticalCombatConfig at capture-plan and quickstep-fixture construction, connected to the server quickstep timing owner.
conditional_findings.connected_repair: Decide and document whether quickstep review intentionally represents a canonical profile or the selected runtime configuration. If it is the selected profile, pass one validated configuration through plan/timing/force/landing construction and preserve explicit fixture mass and deterministic sample behavior; avoid silently changing live tactical authority.
conditional_findings.later_acceptance: After separate implementation and product-validation authorization, compare default and a supported nondefault duration/motor configuration across fixture plan, dodge midpoint and authoritative timing, plus baseline behavior.
conditional_findings.discovery: partial; selected-config semantics, runtime/native outcomes and global aliases open

conditional_findings.severity: unassigned; conditional sample-rate timestamp divergence in source, no report or visual result
conditional_findings.classification: New current-source capture timestamp and sample-rate authority candidate; global alias reconciliation remains open.
conditional_findings.trace: The selected YAML sample_hz is a checked positive AnimationSampleRate and is installed into the runtime snapshot. capture_fixed_clock and capture_frame_elapsed derive the logical fixed interval from that rate. Most scenario constructors record scenario_frame divided by the active rate, but turning_scenario, dynamics_turn_scenario and guard_plant_turn_scenario set time_seconds from frame / 64.0. capture_frame copies this authored value into FrameSample; jitter_frames copies it again, and jitter dt divides observed changes by adjacent timestamp differences. Other report metrics use those same times for durations or facing tracking.
conditional_findings.symbolic_case: With a supported alternate sample_hz = 32.0 and all other canonical settings retained, the selected turn scenario has 65 frames numbered 0 through 64. Its source records frame 64 at 1.0 seconds, while the 64 logical sample intervals from frame 0 to 64 at the active interval 1/32 seconds sum to 2.0 seconds, excluding warmup and wall-clock waiting. Adjacent recorded deltas are 1/64 rather than 1/32. For the same finite measured position change, the selected derivative division would use a denominator half as large; actual bones, incidents and report acceptance have not been produced. At canonical 64 Hz these particular timestamp intervals agree.
conditional_findings.connected_presentation: The manifest records the active sample_hz, while the HTML playback timer and descriptive text explicitly use 64 Hz. At non-64 rates this is a separate presentation consumer of the same rate question; its policy and exact alias are not assumed settled by the timestamp finding. Earlier 059 queue entry 1245 independently identified the non-64-Hz UI/playback question at its original historical revision; it did not establish this 95e timestamp chain or close the alias question.
conditional_findings.first_failed_contract: A captured sample timestamp used for elapsed-time metrics must represent the logical interval actually advanced by the selected capture clock, or be explicitly named as normalized scenario progress.
conditional_findings.canonical_owner: Selected AnimationSampleRate and its derived scenario sample-time/clock boundary, with report playback as a connected consumer.
conditional_findings.connected_repair: Separate normalized turn progress from elapsed sample time and derive timestamps from the selected rate; audit other frame-count assumptions and make playback rate follow its declared report contract, while preserving the intentional 64-sample turn shape and ordinary 64 Hz behavior.
conditional_findings.later_acceptance: After separate implementation and product-validation authorization, compare 32 Hz and 64 Hz runs for timestamps, derivative intervals, scenario progress and report playback, with warmup and intentionally fixed-frame scenarios explicit.
conditional_findings.discovery: partial; full scenario inventory, report presentation policy and global aliases open

existing_contract_connections.trace: The plan and child family inspected here use authored scenario identities and positive explicit speeds for their selected steady calls. The prior unknown-scenario empty-plan assertion remains separately recorded. A generic zero-speed helper input does not by itself establish that a supported built-in plan reaches divide-by-zero; custom sample-rate and selected quickstep configuration are the two bounded current candidates above.
